Dear Partners,

Markets spent the quarter re-learning a lesson they last forgot in the previous cycle: liquidity is not the same thing as value. The policy rate now sits at 5.25%, inflation is holding at 4.1%, and high yield spreads have gapped out to 780bps as default fears resurface across the credit complex. Public equities have entered bear-market territory outright, down -18.0% for the quarter. This is a liquidity event first and a valuation event a distant second — the kind of environment in which mark-to-market vehicles overshoot on the way down, precisely because they must.

Against that backdrop, Meridian's flagship reported a -8.5% return for the quarter, bringing year-to-date performance to -12.0%. Since inception, the portfolio remains at +10.0%, a reminder that the compounding we underwrote in 2021 has not been erased — it has been temporarily obscured. We recognize the -8.5% sits meaningfully better than the -18.0% suffered by public markets this quarter, and we anticipate the question our partners at The Harborlight Pension Trust and others will rightly ask: why the gap? The answer is structural, not evasive. Our portfolio companies are not repriced tick-by-tick by panicked sellers; they are valued on operating fundamentals, discounted cash flows, and comparable transactions that have not yet cleared in this dislocated tape. Private marks lag public repricing by design — that is a feature of the asset class our LPs signed up for, not a flaw we are papering over.
